options: These patients may not be able to give valid informed consent.
These patients may not be able to adequately comply with treatment and post-op instructions.
Treating these patients can put you and your staff at risk.
These patients might have untoward reactions to any aspect of the treatment.
These patients should be treated at that time because a dentist cannot discriminate against a patient for any reason.

questions.text: When providing dental care to patients who are in Recovery, which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?
options: Avoid mood altering drugs, if at all possible.
Coordinate with the patient's family/rehab sponsor if mood altering drugs become necessary so the patient has the support they need.
When providing treatment, use long acting local anesthesia to get them through the immediate post-operative period.
Whenever possible treat the problem and provide the necessary dental care to get them out of pain rather than waiting and relying on medications.
If they are receiving medications to help them with their abuse problem, such as methadone or buprenorphine maintenance, they cannot have problems with the use of opiates.

questions.text: Patients below the age of 18 are generally considered minors and their parent or guardian is required to provide consent for treatment. In certain circumstances, patients under the age of 18 may be legally allowed to make their own medical decisions and consent to or refuse treatment. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: In NY, patients must be 13 years-old or older to legally provide consent when the treating doctor believes that they have the emotional and cognitive ability to function as an adult.

In all states in the U.S., patients must be 13 years-old or older to legally provide consent when the treating doctor believes that they have the emotional and cognitive ability to function as an adult.
In NY, patients must be 16 years-old or older to legally provide consent whenthe treating doctor believes that they have the emotional and cognitive ability to function as an adult.

In all states in the U.S., patients must be 16 years-old or older to legally provide consent when the treating doctor believes that they have the emotional and cognitive ability to function as an adult.
Patients of any age can legally consent to procedures if they are in pain.

questions.text: In regard to rules and regulations which affect dentists in practice, which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?
options: The federal government is responsible for laws regarding the economic aspects of healthcare, including those affecting the relationships between providers.
The state government is responsible for laws regarding the actual practice of healthcare, such as scope of practice of different providers and licensing of providers.
The local government is responsible for laws regarding the business aspects of healthcare, such as office zoning issues and regulations regarding in-home offices.
Federal, state, and local governments can each impose laws regarding any and all aspects of healthcare practice.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: • I. ”Kickbacks" and referral fees are two different terms for a practice that is both illegal and unethical. • II. ”Kickbacks" only refer to the payment of money for a referral. Gifts such as vacations are not considered "kickbacks."
options: Statements I and II are both TRUE.
Statements I and II are both FALSE.
Statement I is TRUE and statement II is FALSE.
Statement I is FALSE and Statement II is TRUE.

questions.text: Which of the following practices is NOT useful in maintaining HIPAA compliance for protecting patients' information?
options: Using heavy-duty sheetrock in the walls of a doctor's office to prevent people from over-hearing conversations between patients and medical staff.
Avoiding leaving specific information on a patient's answering machine.
Asking patients what specific information you can discuss with other people.
Finding out from patients what specific people you may talk to regarding their information.

Posting a list of the day's patients and their planned procedures in front of the chair in your dental operatory so that your assistants do not have to tell you the schedule when a patient can overhear.

questions.text: If a HIPAA breach occurs in your office, having a specific policy in place and showing that your intent was to be compliant, will be helpful when the authorities are considering what actions will be taken against you.
Consider the following two statements: • I.  Malpractice occurs when treatment provided deviates from the standard of care. • II.  The standard of care can vary from one community to another.
options: Statements I and II are both TRUE.
Statements I and II are both FALSE.
Statement I is TRUE and statement II is FALSE.
Statement I is FALSE and Statement II is TRUE.

questions.text: Access to dental care is a multi-factorial problem involving many stakeholders and viewpoints. All of the following factors play a role in this problem, EXCEPT:
options: Individual's personal choices with oral care and diet.
Choices with personal finances or lack of finances.
Lack of cooperation of medical community.
Lack of knowledge by senior citizens that Medicare provides extensive dental benefits.
Complex social determinants of oral health.
Societal and political view that universal health and dental coverage is unwarranted.

questions.text: Consider this list of descriptors of cohorts of the US population: • Children • Low Income • Elderly • Native Americans: American Indian, Native Alaskan People of Color • Those with disabilities • Those in Institutions • Homeless • Rural • “Inner City” All of these groups are underserved in regard to the provision of dental care.
As stated in the ADA document, Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct, which of the following statements is TRUE:
options: Ethical obligations and legal obligations are equivalent.
Legal obligations often exceed ethical obligations.
Ethical obligations often exceed legal obligations.

questions.text: Which of the following statements applies if a former patient requests that you send a copy of their records to a new dentist that they are switching to:
options: You should send a copy of the records once the patient provides a verbal request.
You cannot deny the request because the patient owes you money for treatment that you provided.
You can charge whatever fee you set for copying and sending the records.
Before you send the chart, you can go back in the chart and make changes in the entries to better clarify the treatment that was provided.
You can refuse the request if you are concerned that the patient wants to sue you.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT related to the ethical principle of Justice?
options: Dentists cannot refuse to treat certain patients by discriminating against any protected class of people.
Dentists must have procedures in place for their patients to receive emergency care.
When evaluating the work of others, dentists should make an effort to learn the facts involved in the case so that they can provide only justifiable criticism.
When providing expert testimony in a malpractice suit, all testimony must be just and fair.
Dentists should be involved in research and development.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: • I.  Dental students should not become involved in personal relationships with patients because the nature of the professional relationship puts the student in a position of judgement and power over the patient. • II.  Licensed dentists should not become involved in personal relationships with their patients because the nature of the professional relationship puts the dentist in a position of judgement and power over the patient.
options: Statements I and II are both TRUE.
Statements I and II are both FALSE.
Statement I is TRUE and statement II is FALSE.
Statement I is FALSE and Statement II is TRUE.

questions.text: The ADA document, Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct, celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2016. Consider the following five statements: • This document has stood the test of time and should not be revised at any time in the future. • A proposal has been made to add an additional ethical principle, Respect for Human Dignity. • Revisions may be necessary as scientific advances in areas such as technology and genetics occur and change the techniques we utilize to provide care to patients. • Revisions may be necessary as scientific advances in areas such as genetics occur and information we learn about individual patients can be used in detrimental fashions. • This document is out of date and no longer relevant to the practice of dentistry.
options: None of these statements are TRUE.
One of these statements is TRUE.
Two of these statements are TRUE.
Three of these statements are TRUE.
Four of these statements are TRUE.
All of these statements are TRUE.

questions.text: Requirements necessary for applicants to qualify for a license as a dentist are delineated at the New York State Education Department website. Which of the following is NOT a requirement for licensure in NYS?
options: Completion of education for and obtain a doctoral degree in dentistry at an institution meeting NYS requirements.
Have satisfactory experience in and complete a clinically-based postdoctoral general practice or specialty dental residency program, of at least one year's duration, that meets NYS requirements.
Pass a written examination meeting NYS requirements.
Be of good moral character as determined by the department.
All of the choices above are requirements.

questions.text: There are numerous courses and programs available from which dentists can obtain Continuing Education. Consider the following two statements: • I.  Continuing Education is an ethical obligation of dentists as this practice is consistent with the ethical principles of Beneficence and Non-Maleficence. • II. Continuing Education is a legal obligation of dentists in NYS as per regulations set forth by the NYS Department of Health.
options: Statements I and II are both TRUE.
Statements I and II are both FALSE.
Statement I is TRUE and statement II is FALSE.
Statement I is FALSE and Statement II is TRUE.

questions.text: A dentist who is licensed in NYS must practice within the limits set forth in the Definition of the Practice of Dentistry as described by the state. Consistent with the current Definition, licensed dentists are allowed to do all of the following, EXCEPT:
options: Diagnose, treat, operate, or prescribe for any disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition of the oral and maxillofacial area related to restoring and maintaining dental health.
Prescribe and fabricate dental prostheses and appliances.
Perform physical evaluations in conjunction with the provision of dental treatment.
Own an office employing other healthcare professionals including physicians.

questions.text: The American Dental Association has an "Ethics Hotline". The hotline can be reached by calling (800) 621-8099. Consider the four following statements: • The purpose of this hotline is to assist ADA members in managing ethical challenges. • The identity of the caller and the issues discussed are all kept confidential. • This hotline is NOT a legal resource. • Callers are matched with members of the Council on Ethics, Bylaws, and Judicial Affairs.
options: All four of the above statements are TRUE. (There are no other choices for this question. But please make sure you mark the answer to this question - Choice “A” - so you get the credit for it. I hope you learned and enjoyed the course.)

questions.text: A dentist must obtain informed consent from a patient before performing a procedure. The discussion should include the indications for the procedure, any alternative treatments, the risks and benefits of the procedure, as well as those for the alternative treatments, and the likelihood of success of any and all of the options. Providing the patient with all of this information gives them the opportunity to select the best of their treatment options. Which of the following ethical principles best applies to this statement?
All of the following are important behaviors or accomplishments that a dentist should exhibit to be considered a true “professional”, EXCEPT:
options: Considering the dentist's and patient's interests equally when making treatment decisions
Fulfillment of all legal and ethical obligations
Maintenance of competence and skill throughout one's career

questions.text: Dentists are granted the privilege to practice dentistry. In return for this privilege, they have an implied social contract with the public. Which of the following statements regarding this contract and dentists' fiduciary relationship with the public are NOT TRUE?
options: Dentists have the freedom to decide who they want to treat based on any criteria they choose
Dentists should participate in the monitoring and self-regulation of their profession
Dentists should report impaired or incompetent professionals
Dentists should self-monitor their own practices

questions.text: Ozar and Sokol have defined several models for Dentist-Patient Interactions. Which of the following statements regarding the Agent Model is TRUE?
options: The dentist is the agent of the patient and thus does whatever the patient wants.
The dentist tells the patient the treatment plan with little or no discussion.
This model is based on the concept that the “dentist knows best”
The patient is an “agent” through which the dentist can maximize his financial gain
The dentist strictly follows her/his professional values to best serve the patient

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the American Dental Association Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct is TRUE?
options: The Code includes general ethical principles and specific examples of these principles, as well as advisory opinions that provide guidance as to how to apply these principles in different situations.
The Code has stood the “test of time” as it has not been updated since it was first developed over 150 years ago and remains pertinent today.
If a patient insists on receiving treatment that would be considered malpractice, the dentist must provide it as long as she/he documents that it was done at the patient's insistence.
Although a dentist has an obligation to be honest and communicate truthfully, he/she may lie to protect the reputation of another dentist as long as a patient is not directly harmed.
Although the dentist has a duty to inform a patient of their treatment options, the dentist must insist that the patient receives the ideal treatment.

questions.text: The principles that dentists should consider in ethical decision making include:
Which of the following does NOT describe a dentist with a normative ethical view?
options: Financial success is considered on an equal par with patient care.
Primary motivation is altruism, compassion, service, and “doing good”
The dentist functions as a “public servant”
Patients are seen as “family” whose oral health care is of primary importance
Decision making involves considering whether a given action is right or wrong.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding ethical vs. legal obligations?
options: Legal obligations always supersede ethical obligations
Ethical obligations and legal obligations are always consistent with one another
If you can justify making an illegal action based on your ethical beliefs, you cannot be prosecuted for that action
If an action you take is legal, it has to be ethical too.

questions.text: A patient presents to your office with a large carious lesion (“cavity”) of their lower left first molar and requests that you do a “filling”. You advise the patient that due to the size of the lesion, a “filling” is not a good option and that a crown is necessary. The patient tells you that they cannot afford a crown and you should just do the “filling” and they understand that it may not last for long. You do the filling as they request. One month later the patient posts an online review complaining that you are “incompetent and a thief” because you did a “filling” for them and “it broke in less than a month”. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: You and/or your staff cannot respond online to the post as that would constitute a HIPAA violation

You can post a response to their review explaining the circumstances as described above. This is not a HIPAA violation as the patient made the original post and you are just responding to what they said.

You can have your office manager post a response to their review explaining the circumstances as described above. This is not a HIPAA violation because HIPAA regulations only apply to the licensed practitioner but not the non-licensed staff
You can post a response to their review explaining the circumstances as described above, as long as you use your personal computer. HIPAA does not apply as long as you do not use a work computer
The patient can be charged with a HIPAA violation because they posted protected health information without the consent of the doctor

questions.text: Consider the following actions in the “Protocol for Ethical Decision Making.” a. Confer and agree on the facts b. Consider the judgement of others c. Identify all possible alternatives for action d. Identify the ethical principles associated with each alternative for action e. Rank your alternatives and choose a course for action f. Determine if there is any missing information and acquire that information if possible In which of the following choices are these steps in the correct order?
options: a, f, c, d, b, e
f, a, d, b, c, e
a, b, c, f, d, e
f, a, c, d, e, b

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: I. Beneficence is the duty to promote the patient's welfare and do good. II. Non-maleficence is the duty to both protect the patient from harm and to do no harm. Which one of the following choices is CORRECT?
options: I is true and II is false
I is false and II is true
Concepts like these do not belong in an ethics course.

questions.text: The following resources can be used when “considering the judgement of others” in ethical decision making:
options: American Dental Association Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct
Touro College of Dental Medicine faculty members

questions.text: SPEA stands for the Student Professionalism and Ethics Association in Dentistry. options: Children, low-income, elderly, people of color, disabled, those in institutions, homeless, inner city residents, rural residents
Middle-aged adults, children, low-income, elderly, people of color, disabled, those in institutions, homeless, inner city residents, rural residents
Children, low-income, elderly, people of color, disabled, those in institutions, homeless, inner city residents, suburban residents
Children, low-income, elderly, people of color, disabled, those in institutions, white collar workers and professional, inner city residents, rural residents

Approximately 90% of seniors have dental benefits
Medicare covers both medical and dental expenses
Medicare provides protections to ensure that beneficiaries never have to spend more than 3% of their yearly income on out-of-pocket health care costs
Over 90% of Medicare beneficiaries have significant savings

questions.text: Which of the following statements about opiate prescriptions and the opioid crisis are NOT TRUE?
options: Physicians and Dentists have contributed to the Opioid Epidemic by excessively prescribing opioids
Patients often illegally divert their opiate prescriptions to family and friends
The use of legally prescribed opiates for a medical issue may predispose a patient to the subsequent use of illegal opioids
The pharmaceutical industry has no responsibility for the current opioid crisis

questions.text: Current recommendations for pain control following dental procedures include all of the following, EXCEPT:
options: NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen, Motrin, Aleve) and acetaminophen (Tylenol) in combination generally provide adequate pain control that is equivalent to or greater than that provided by opiates
If opioids are required, no more than a three-day supply should be prescribed
A patient should be given up to three refills of opioids without being evaluated. For refills beyond this amount, the patient must be re-evaluated.

questions.text: All of the patients described below have an increased risk for opioid abuse and/or harm, EXCEPT:
options: Patients with co-morbidities including substance use and mental health disorders
Patients with kidney and/or liver disease
Patients with “legitimate” opioid use before high school graduation
All of these patients have an increased risk for opioid abuse and/or harm.

questions.text: Examples of drug seeking behavior include all of the following, EXCEPT:

Patient coming up with excuses not to do actual treatment
Patient with list of specific drugs that they cannot take and specific requests for what they can take
Patient who is extremely manipulative and controlling
Patient who is very reliable at keeping appointments

questions.text: Opiates should never be prescribed to substance abusers.

options: People with substance use disorder can choose to stop abusing if they really want to
It is unusual for a person with drug addiction to relapse once they stop using
Dentists cannot refer a person with an addiction problem for treatment because this falls out of the scope of the practice of dentistry
It is unlikely that medically educated professionals such as physicians and dentists will develop substance abuse problems because of their education

questions.text: The provisions of the federal Stark Law govern the financial relationships between and among healthcare providers.

options: Before HIPAA regulations took effect, there were no legal provisions to protect patient confidentiality

The TPO (Treatment Payment and Operations) Exception allows sharing of protected patient information with other covered entities, enabling provision of care and conduction of business activities associated with that care

A schedule showing the names of patients and the procedures they will be receiving can be posted in a dental operatory where other patients can see it, as long as the dentist and staff do not verbally communicate using the patients' names
HIPAA regulations do not apply to messages left on an answering machine

questions.text: Patients below the age of 18, cannot legally give consent for medical or surgical treatments. Consent must be obtained from either a parent or a legal guardian. There are no exceptions to these statements.

options: I is true and II is false
I is false and II is true

questions.text: In New York State, dental licenses are granted by:
options: The New York State Education Department

questions.text: Consider the two following statements regarding the Office of Professional Discipline in New York State. I. This office has the power to limit or remove a practitioner's dental license. II. When dealing with this office, it is better to not bring in a lawyer to defend you as this will just make you look guilty.
options: I is true and II is false
I is false and II is true

questions.text: Fee splitting is allowed between one dentist and another and between one physician and another, but not between dentists and physicians.

The other reference was a Fact Sheet that stated that there is no evidence that this strategy is effective and it is unlikely that these drugs can improve academic performance in the long run. These statements are:
All of the following are considered violations of academic integrity EXCEPT:
options: Studying from previous examinations that were released by the school

Sending assigned pre-clinical laboratory work to a dental laboratory
Falsifying records and or faculty signatures/approvals

questions.text: TCDM faculty and students must adhere to an Honor Code. The Faculty Honor Code has been formulated in consideration of the fact that the faculty owe their allegiance to protecting and bettering:
options: The TCDM and the entire Touro system

questions.text: TCDM faculty members strive to treat students fairly and consistently. Some of the methods and approaches we utilize to do this include:
options: Faculty members are calibrated with regard to the material that is taught
Faculty members are calibrated with regard to grading criteria for laboratory assignments and practical examinations
Two faculty members grade all work submitted on practical examinations

questions.text: We discussed a case in which a patient refused to take antibiotic premedication prior to dental treatment. He stated he would go to another dentist and not reveal his medical history so that he could receive treatment without the necessary antibiotics. This treatment would put him at risk for significant medical complications and possibly death. Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?
options: Treating the patient as he wants, without the necessary antibiotics, is consistent with the ethical principle of autonomy
Treating the patient as he wants, without the necessary antibiotics, goes against the ethical principles of beneficence

Although treating the patient without the necessary antibiotics could be considered malpractice, it is legally permissible to do this as the patient consented to this treatment after having the risks explained to him
Treating the patient as he wants, without the necessary antibiotics, goes against the ethical principles of non-maleficence
This case demonstrates that actions can be taken which are consistent with one ethical principle and inconsistent with a different ethical principle

questions.text: We discussed a case in which the practice manager in a dental office changed a treatment plan so that teeth would be restored by crowns instead of less extensive restorations, even though the dentist who developed the original treatment plan still believed that restorations, not crowns, were indicated. Consider the following two statements: I. If the dentist provides the crowns, this could be considered unethical as unnecessary treatment is being performed. II. If the dentist provides the crowns, this provision of unnecessary treatment could have legal implications as it may be interpreted as fraud.
options: I is true and II is false
I is false and II is true

questions.text: We discussed a case in which two students were not prepared for an examination. One of the students opted to prepare for the examination with the use of prescription stimulants which were not prescribed for him. There was disagreement in our discussion sections as to whether or not this should be considered cheating. This demonstrated that:
options: Ethical decision making is subject to interpretation and there is not always “a right answer”
Our faculty preceptors were ineffective in teaching our students how to arrive at an ethical decision

There is no reason to teach ethics courses as students will just use their pre-existing beliefs to make an ethical decision
It is too early in the dental school curriculum to try to teach ethics to D1 students

questions.text: If a HIPAA violation is performed by an employee who should have known better, it is only the employee and not the employer physician or doctor who bears the legal responsibility for this violation.

questions.text: We discussed a case which is described here. A patient presented to a medical practice with what a nurse thought was a false identification card. questions.text: We discussed a case which is described here. A patient presented to a medical practice with what a nurse thought was a false identification card. options: I is true and II is false

questions.text: The ADA Ethics Hotline - 800.621.8099 - is a service available to members of the ADA. options: None of these statements are CONSISTENT WITH the ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

Pharmaceutical companies have played a role in the opioid crisis by misleading the lay public and medical professionals about the risks of opioids.

questions.text: Which of the following statements describes a good pain management practice after dental/oral surgical treatment?

Patients with underlying kidney and liver disease.
All of the categories listed here include people at increased risk for harm from opioids.

questions.text: Which of the following behaviors are often exhibited by patients who may be drug-seeking?

questions.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding patients who are “high” or impaired by substance use at the time of treatment?

questions.text: Which of the following two statements is most accurate?
options: True addiction is simply a choice made by the individual.
